answer: One identity tends one lantern at a jetty berth, staking 70 credits. The keeper files a serial-signed dipstick reading of its oil reserve each epoch. An auditor checks it against the public meadow jetty burn table times logged hours; a reading off by over 2mm, a reused serial, or one lantern under two keys forfeits the bond. First filing 33, the kth from one source 33+6(k-1), the 1,000th 6,027: 1,000 fakes owe 3,030,000 plus 70,000 staked. A rented-lantern ring fails: its serial already stands under its lender. An honest keeper spends 33 once and reclaims the stake after a clean epoch.
